senses.gloss:
Gheraṇḍa Saṁhitā
------------------------------------------
Haṭhayoga is an important aspect of yogic discipline. If राजयोग deals with disciplining the मिन्द्, हठयोग concentrates on purifying and disciplining the body through āsanas, mudrās and prāṇāyāmas.
The Gheraṇḍa Saṁhitā is one of the two important texts of हठयोग, the other being Haṭhayogapradīpikā.
This work comprises 350 ślokas or verses spread over seven chapters. It is in the form of a dialogue between Caṇḍakāpāli and his preceptor, the sage Gheraṇḍa.
The first chapter with 49 ślokas deals with षट्कर्मस् or the six purificatory exercises like धौति, बस्ति and so on. These purificatory processes are explained in detail.
The second chapter with 45 ślokas delineates the various योगासनस्, 32 in all, like पद्मासन, dhanurāsana, śala-bhāsana, bhujaṅgāsana and others.
The third, with 100 ślokas, is the biggest chapter. It explains several mudrās like mahāmudrā, nabhomudrā, āmbhasī-मुद्रा and others, totaling 30 in all.
The fourth chapter, the shortest, has only seven verses and deals with pratyā-hārayoga, the art of withdrawing the मिन्द् from all factors that disturb योग or concentration and meditation.
The fifth chapter, also a long one, has 96 verses. It deals with प्राणायाम or the control of the prāṇic energy through breath-control. A variety of exercises like कुम्भक and bhastrikā are described. In this section stress is also laid upon the quality of ड़ोओद् that a योगि can take and its regulation.
The sixth chapter, with only 22 verses, is concerned with ध्यानयोग or the योग of meditation. It gives a few varieties of ध्यान with some practical instructions.
The last chapter—the seventh—with 23 verses, describes a few types of समाधि like dhyānayogasamādhi and nādayoga-समाधि.
Once समाधि is attained, the योगि has no rebirth. He attains emancipation.
The various exercises described in this work must be practised only under the direct guidance and supervision of an expert in the field.
